OPT-IN + safe: the hook is silent when nothing is activated, NEVER trains, always exits 0 (fail-open). This restores full parity with the two retired plugins (TRAIN + USE) entirely under `/domain`. 0.11.0 (2026-06-07) ML subverbs unify the retired `skillopt` + `skillopt-hook` plugins under `/domain`: `/domain doctor` (skill-train readiness) · `/domain train [--bg]` (NATIVE pip-free SkillOpt loop — rollout → reflect → edit → held-out gate via `claude -p` = your Claude Code subscription, NOT a metered API; only a SEPARATE skill.md is optimized — the domain's own DOMAIN.md / verdicts / log are NEVER touched) · `consume <skill.md>` · `activate`/`deactivate` (write ~/.sidecar/domain-skill/active-skill.md) · `status`/`log`. Bundled `examples/toyqa` (6 format-sensitive QA items) proves the loop end-to-end with NO external data/pip. ML verbs route to `bin/_domain_ml.sh` (+ `bin/_domain_ml.py` engine); ALL existing domain verbs route to `_domain.hexa` UNCHANGED. 0.10.1 (2026-06-03) `_is_name` now accepts a DIGIT-LEADING NAME — first char may be an UPPERCASE letter OR a digit 0-9, so `/domain init 8VERB` works (previously rejected: digit-leading start); subsequent chars unchanged (UPPERCASE/digit/`-`/`+`). 0.10.0 — bare `/domain` + `/domain list` now LINT for scattered report-like `.md` (a basename token audit|report|verdict|gap|finding|impl OR an ISO date like `2026-06-02`) sitting loose at the repo root or under `docs/` WHILE a domain is active, and emit a `⚠ 분리보관 감지` advisory naming each stray with its `/domain absorb <file>` runbook (excludes the domain's own pair / CHANGELOG / README / `.log.md` / already-absorbed pointer files; read-only). 0.9.0 — new `absorb <file> [--state]` verb enforces combined-storage (합산보관) over scattered docs/*.md: folds an existing separate report/finding `.md` into the ACTIVE domain's single doc pair (default → <NAME>.log.md as a dated `## <ISO> — absorbed <rel>` entry embedding the body; `--state` → <NAME>.md snapshot), then replaces the source with a one-line `<!-- absorbed into … -->` pointer (idempotent — an already-absorbed pointer file is skipped; refuses to absorb the domain's own pair). Resolves the active domain via the same _get_active / _snap_path / _log_path logic the other verbs use. Maintain UPPERCASE <NAME>.md (snapshot = final-goal milestone checkboxes) + sister <NAME>.log.md (append-only step log) at project root — auto-scaffolds both, defaults NAME to uppercase basename of git root. Verbs: /domain <NAME> (SELECT the session's active domain → later verbs default to it + show a final-goal progress bar `▓▓▓░░ NN% · done/total` from the snapshot's checkboxes) · /domain (show active) · /domain list (alias ls — repo-wide index; with a DOMAINS.tape roster it is AUTHORITATIVE: tables each registered domain ★ = active · @goal · progress · location, progress/@goal stay DERIVED so the checked-in roster holds only NAME→path and never churns; flags ghosts + unregistered; no roster → legacy disk-scan) · /domain list --sync (reconcile DOMAINS.tape with disk — bootstraps the roster) · /domain <task> (append `- [x]` to log) · /domain todo <task> (`- [ ]`) · /domain done <match> (flip [ ]→[x]) · /domain title <text> (alias subtitle — OPTIONAL `@title:` display header: icon · name · alias, e.g. `🧠 IIT4 — 의식 측정자(尺)`, rendered in place of plain `active domain: NAME`; absence keeps current output, no lint warning) · /domain new <header>. Progress is final-goal-based (snapshot completion), not log-based — it doesn't drift as the log grows. Path resolution: a DOMAINS.tape roster row (`@domain NAME := "path"`) wins FIRST, so a domain can live at ANY path (e.g. `domains/RUNTIME/RUNTIME.md`); absent a roster entry it falls back to root → folder-nested → root-default-scaffold (log follows the snapshot's dir), so folder-nested meta-domains no longer regenerate an empty root scaffold each call. The folder-nested fallback only matches when the nested file's first line is the domain header `# <NAME>` (guards against false-matching an unrelated same-named file like a digest on case-insensitive filesystems). 0.8.8: /domain set now SELF-HEALS the DOMAINS.tape roster (auto-registers an on-disk-but-unregistered domain — the gap that ghosted anima's LIFE) and warns on a stale SSOT shadow (the working-tree <NAME>.md is UNTRACKED or BEHIND origin/main → progress/closure may read a stale local copy; reference_domain_init_untracked_ssot); a perpetual `@goal` (no-termination marker like `종료 조건 없음`/`perpetual`/`open horizon`) renders a ♾️ perpetual badge so the progress bar reads as frontier-depletion, NOT a 100% completion countdown (per feedback-closure-is-physical-limit).
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: domain-doc-guard
plugins.desc: 0.1.0 — PostToolUse(Write|Edit) advisory enforcing combined-storage (합산보관) over scattered docs/*.md: when a report-like `.md` is written WHILE a domain is active, it nudges the model to fold the file into the active domain's single doc pair (`<DOMAIN>.md` + `<DOMAIN>.log.md`) via `domain absorb`, instead of leaving it scattered as a separate doc. Implemented in hexa-lang (`_domain_doc_guard.hexa`, invoked via `hexa run`). FIRES (exit 2, non-blocking additionalContext) only when BOTH hold: (1) the written file is a `.md` whose basename or first ~40 content lines match a report heuristic — a token (audit|report|verdict|gap|finding|impl) OR an ISO date like `2026-06-02`; AND (2) a domain is CURRENTLY ACTIVE for this (repo-root × session), read from the same `$HOME/.claude/domain-active.tsv` store `domain set` writes (exact (root,session) row, else the most-recent any-session row for the root). SILENT (exit 0) otherwise — a plain `notes.md`, a non-`.md`, the active domain's own `<DOMAIN>.md` / `*.log.md` / CHANGELOG / README, an already-absorbed pointer file, or when NO domain is active (so it never fires in a fresh repo / a sub-shell with no domain context). De-dupes once per (session, file) via a CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA marker. Pairs with the `domain` plugin's `absorb` verb (the runbook it points at). Advisory-only (per guards-narrow-scope). NO opt-out by design.
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: domain-cycle-guard
plugins.desc: 0.1.0 — Stop|SubagentStop (cycle-close) enforcement that the ACTIVE domain's doc pair (`<DOMAIN>.md` + `<DOMAIN>.log.md`) is updated EVERY CYCLE, so per-cycle progress is never lost and the domain SSOT never goes stale (매 사이클 도메인 문서 업데이트 강제). Sibling of the advisory `domain-doc-guard` (same family): that one folds a SCATTERED report `.md` INTO the domain; this one catches the inverse — work happened this cycle but the domain doc was NEVER touched. Implemented in hexa-lang (`_domain_cycle_guard.hexa`, via `hexa run`). At cycle-close: (1) resolve the ACTIVE domain for (repo-root × session) from the same `$HOME/.claude/domain-active.tsv` store `domain set` writes + its snapshot path from `DOMAINS.tape` (both roster forms `@domain NAME := "path"` and `@D NAME := "path" :: domain`); none/unregistered → SILENT no-op. (2) detect work-this-cycle CHEAPLY — `git status --porcelain` (dirty tree) ∪ files newer than a per-(root,session) cycle-start marker; no work → SILENT. (3) if `<DOMAIN>.md` OR `<DOMAIN>.log.md` is among the touched files → SILENT (compliant). (4) work happened BUT domain doc untouched → ENFORCE: DEFAULT advisory-strong `systemMessage` (never hard-traps the user), telling the agent to append a `<DOMAIN>.log.md` step / flip a milestone before closing; HARD-BLOCK opt-in via env `DOMAIN_CYCLE_GUARD_HARD=1` or marker `~/.claude/domain-cycle-guard.hard` emits the harness Stop block decision `{decision:block}` instead. Honors `stop_hook_active` (never loops). The cycle-start marker is refreshed after every close (work / no-work / enforce) so each cycle measures relative to the prior close — one enforce per cycle window. Stop is harness-reachable for plugins (verdict-gate + celebrate already register Stop hooks). Gate is a real precondition (active domain + work + doc untouched), not an opt-out switch.
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: go
plugins.desc: /go [hint] — proceed with the most-recently proposed action / continue the paused flow without further confirmation. Bare "go" single-word user message also catches as natural-language alias. Identical semantics to '그냥 진행해' / 'continue' / 'just run it' — re-read the last agent message, identify what was proposed/paused/awaiting (a plan · a recommended option · the next /sbs step · the next /cycle round · a /cycle-fg halted item · an AskUserQuestion default), and execute it verbatim. Optional `/go <hint>` disambiguates (e.g. `/go ubu-2` selects host, `/go retry` re-fires a failed step, `/go skip` advances past, `/go all` applies to every candidate). NO new plan, NO re-question — stateless continuation token. If no recent proposal exists, ask one short line rather than fabricate. Distinct from /sbs (plan-first sequential) and /cycle (autonomous fan-out): /go is a token, not a runbook. Triggers — '/go', bare 'go' (single-word), '진행', '계속', '다음 진행', 'proceed', 'continue', 'ok go', 'yes go'.
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: roi
plugins.desc: /roi [scope] — enumerate LOSSLESS performance/resource/speed improvement candidates as a ranked TODO list. "Lossless" = no functional regression, no API breakage, no semantic change, no test failures — only HOW the same behavior is achieved more efficiently. Scope: bare /roi = active domain (if set) ELSE cwd repo · /roi <message> restricts to that scope (file path · subdirectory · feature name · layer · language · hot path). Output is a single ranked table `| # | category | item | impact | effort | risk | how | evidence |` where category ∈ {⚡ speed · 🧠 perf (CPU/algo) · 💾 resource (mem/disk/network) · 🔋 efficiency}, sorted by impact-to-effort ratio (highest ROI first), risk=low ONLY (any candidate that could risk behavior change is dropped — that's NOT lossless). Discovery: scope read → anti-pattern grep (N+1, re-parse-per-call, O(n²) where O(n log n) trivially applies, unbounded growth, sync I/O on hot path, sort+take-1 vs min, regex recompile per loop, dict lookup not hoisted, …) → bench-ground claims where measurable (@D bench_kernel_choices, 가정 말고 벤치) → rank. Cap default top 10/category. Drop-count surfaced when items excluded for risk≥medium. Triggers — '/roi', '/roi <scope>', 'roi 뽑아', 'roi list', '무손실 개선 할일', '성능 개선 할일', '자원 개선 할일', '속도 개선 할일', '효율 개선 할일', 'lossless improvements', 'perf wins'.
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: gap
plugins.desc: /gap — multi-axis gap exploration. 42 breakthrough-strategy lenses · 8 families (F4 + F6 each have 6 lenses; `occams-razor` lives in both — hypothesis side and design side). Bare /gap = inline-triage + deep-dive only hot families. /gap full = exhaustive 8-subagent fan-out. /gap <scope> targets the sweep. /gap list prints the catalogue. Surfaces + prioritises gaps; never fixes.
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: sidecar
plugins.desc: 0.11.0 — `sync` realign GUARD: the realign (`git checkout main` + `reset --hard origin/main`) targets ONLY the hx-managed marketplace clone (`~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/sidecar`) and runs ONLY when the tree carries nothing to lose. A pure precondition gate `_sync_realign_decision()` REALIGNs only when the repo IS the marketplace clone (a user dev checkout at a different path, or carrying a `.sidecar-dev` marker, is SKIPPED), the tree is clean, AND HEAD is on `main` or a non-main branch with NO unpushed commits ahead of origin/main (an ahead branch holds in-flight work → SKIP). Concurrent `sidecar sync` callers serialize on a short mkdir lock. No env opt-out (s11). New `sidecar sync-guard-selftest` proves the 4 cases on throwaway repos (clean-on-main → REALIGN · clean-on-feature-ahead → SKIP · dirty → SKIP · dev-checkout → SKIP). Protects a shared dev checkout from being yanked to main by the post-ship `sidecar sync` / auto-sync hook; the `fuse` launchd daemon is a separate circuit, untouched. 0.10.0 — `fuse` FREEZE-IMMINENT tier (@L4 · mini kernel-panic 2026-06-02): a new MEM_HARD_PCT (default 92 · above the mem_pct admission line) tier SIGKILLs the single largest non-claude memory consumer INCLUDING active hexa runs — this tier ALONE drops the 'never touch active hexa runs' exemption (that exemption is what let a 76GB runaway hexa_run starve WindowServer into a watchdog panic) while STILL never touching claude (s9) or sshd. New fuse_top_mem_hexa() selector + mem_hard_pct config key; `fuse selftest` extended to prove the hexa_run reap spares sshd/claude with zero freeze risk. /sidecar <args> — thin wrapper over the `sidecar` marketplace CLI (host-local, on PATH via `hx install sidecar`). 0.9.0 — `fuse` mem-reap: a MEM trip now SIGTERM-REAPS the top-RSS (memory) consumer to actually RECLAIM RAM (renice only lowers CPU priority — frees no pages — so a mem-trip renice could not stop a memory freeze; that was the bug behind a 5GB balloon → mem 99% → sshd starved → SSH banner never sent). cpu/load trips keep the reversible renice. The reap target excludes claude (s9), sshd (NEVER reaped — keeping SSH alive is the point), and self/hexa/awk/ps; the mem reclaim is mandatory, no opt-out (s11). New `fuse selftest` proves the reap on a ulimit-capped synthetic sleeper hog while sparing sshd/claude-named processes, with zero freeze risk. 0.8.1 — `mirror` now SKIPS fully-orphaned/superseded plugins: it picks the highest NON-orphaned cache version (every version carrying `.orphaned_at` → plugin deprecated → not command-mirrored), so a renamed plugin's stale command no longer double-surfaces in the TUI alongside its successor (e.g. the `system`→`lab` rename: orphaned `system` was still emitting `~/.claude/commands/system.md`). Generic — no plugin name hard-coded. 0.8.0 — NEW `handoff` verb: the cross-project handoff registry (~/.sidecar/handoff/handoff.jsonl, single SSOT for cross-repo gap/patch/bug/RFC handoffs per commons g11·g36·g48·g59·g60; retires the per-repo INBOX domain). `handoff add <repo> <text...>` appends an open JSONL entry · `handoff ls [<repo>]` tables entries (filter by repo) · `handoff done <id>` flips status → done · bare `handoff` prints a counts summary. JSONL not markdown (structured carrier · project.tape s2); store is repo-external runtime state, portable via $HOME; atomic tmp+rename writes. 0.7.0 — `reap` verb (reap stale `hexa-lsp` idle > 2h; dry-run by default, `reap --kill` terminates; never touches claude @D s9 or active hexa runs) + `paths add/rm` SIGN-GATED (key `paths`: `! sidecar sign paths` first, since the whitelist overrides pool-route). Verbs — init (scaffold project.tape + CLAUDE.md symlink + LATTICE_POLICY.md) · sync (pull marketplace + refresh cache + installed_plugins.json + enable plugins + mirror commands) · mirror (refresh ~/.claude/commands/ mirrors so plugin commands are bare-invocable — `Skill("imagine")` instead of `Skill("imagine:imagine")` — auto-runs at sync tail) · shadow [plan] (drop the FORCED `plugin:command` namespace #15882 — mirror+disable every command/skill plugin, splicing SKILL.md triggers into the bare command so it stays lossless; hook/mcp kept; `plan` = dry-run; re-asserted at sync tail) · unshadow (revert) · paths (0.6.0 NEW — manage the LOCAL-EXECUTION WHITELIST `~/.sidecar/local-paths`; pool-route 0.10.0 forces any Bash cmd whose argv contains a `/`-prefixed token starting with a registered prefix to run LOCAL. `paths` lists, `paths add` registers cwd, `paths add <dir>` registers an abs-resolved dir (refuses non-existent / already-present), `paths rm <prefix>` removes a line by exact match. Seeded on first use with `~/.claude/plugins/cache/sidecar/` + `~/core/sidecar/`. Atomic writes; whitelist itself IS the opt-in — no env opt-out — @D s11 safe.) · sign (user sign-off gate). `sign <key>` mints a 5-min token at ~/.sidecar/signs/<key>.sign unlocking agent edits to a sign-gated governance SSOT file — the sign-guard hook hard-denies those edits until a fresh token exists; keys are `commons` (commons.tape), `project` (project.tape), `gitignore` (.gitignore), and `paths` (~/.sidecar/local-paths). Bare `sign` / `sign --list` shows active tokens; `sign clear [<key>]` removes them. Multi-user enable profiles — `profile [<name>]` shows/sets the enable profile (minimal = core only · hexa = core + hexa-lang · full = everything, default · master = full + creator-only). `master [on|off|status]` mints/removes the ~/.sidecar/master marker. `enable`/`disable <plugin>` force one plugin on/off (per-plugin override), `reset <plugin>` drops the override; each re-applies the install. State in ~/.sidecar/profile + plugin-overrides.json; install.hexa enables per .claude-plugin/profiles.json tiers — plugin disable, not an in-guard opt-out (@D s11 safe). Args pass through unchanged.
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: watch
plugins.desc: /watch <video-url-or-path> [question] — give Claude the ability to watch a video. Downloads with yt-dlp (YouTube · TikTok · X · Instagram · Vimeo · local file), extracts auto-scaled frames with ffmpeg (2 fps / 100-frame hard cap, duration-aware budget; --start/--end for a denser focused window), pulls a timestamped transcript native-captions-first, then hands frames + transcript to Claude so it answers grounded in what's on screen and in the audio. Whisper API fallback is OPTIONAL — captions-only works keyless and a missing key degrades to frames-only, never hard-fails; the key is read env → sidecar `secret` CLI (macOS Keychain `groq.api_key`/`openai.api_key`) → ~/.config/watch/.env. SessionStart hook surfaces a one-line setup status; setup.py auto-installs ffmpeg/yt-dlp (brew on macOS). Ported to sidecar from bradautomates/claude-video@c333c22 (plugin `watch` v0.1.3, MIT, Bradley Bonanno).
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: inject
plugins.desc: Immediately inject the latest sidecar commons.tape + project.tape into the CURRENT session and sync the local install for the next session. /inject (and `/ij` short alias) runs `sidecar sync` (marketplace pull + cache copy + installed_plugins.json patch) AND prints the current commons.tape + (cwd's) project.tape so the model picks them up this turn. 0.2.1 (2026-05-30) fixes a command-flattening bug — the `!`-command was newline-separated, but when the harness flattens it to one line `set -e` swallowed the rest (`set -e sidecar sync echo …`), breaking the run; rewritten as a single `;`/`&&`-separated line that works flattened, dropping `set -e`.
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: ship
plugins.desc: Atomic ship tail for sidecar plugin changes — /ship -m "<msg>" <path>... stages explicit paths (never -A/-u), credential-scans the staged diff (rpa_ · sk- · hf_ · AKIA), commits, pushes origin/<branch>, then runs `sidecar sync` (marketplace pull + cache copy + installed_plugins.json patch). Mechanical tail of @D ship / commons g27; the agent owns version bump + surface lockstep + message FIRST. Bare /ship (no -m / no paths) is helper mode (0.3.2): lists uncommitted changes + emits a ready-to-edit `/ship -m "..." <paths>` template instead of a usage error, exits 0, still never auto-stages. NL trigger via skill (ship · 배포 · 출시).
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: bypass
plugins.desc: Anti-punt — DEFAULT BEHAVIOR (auto-fires, not opt-in). Universal self-check before any move that hands control back to the user (interactive input · unauthorized destructive · external visible · explicit user-review request); if all NO, just execute. Extensible catalog of patterns: 'next user action:' blocks · 'Should I proceed?' confirmations · 'Want me to check?' deferrals · option-trees with obvious default · over-clarification · defer-by-waiting · excessive recap. Cross-project always-on enforcement in commons.tape ≥0.7.3.
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: brainstorm
plugins.desc: Iterative brainstorming — given a seed, generates ideas in rounds and keeps going until depletion (no genuinely new ideas vs prior rounds; hard cap 8 rounds). For breadth over selection. Skill (natural language) + /brainstorm command.
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: easy
plugins.desc: Easy (friendly) response style — 7-element pattern (icon · name · alias · plain-line · analogy · ASCII · compare). Skill (natural-language trigger) + /easy command. 5 language samples: en · ko · ja · zh · ru. /easy command body now points at $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT with a cache-resolved fallback (0.1.2) so the bare-invocable user-level mirror works. 0.1.3 — layperson+ASCII 강화 (easy-auto 0.3.0 미러): 5개 언어 styles 에 ASCII 구조 4종 템플릿 + 일반인 gold(전문용어→생활어) + 번역 체크리스트 + 측정 축 ascii-structure-template-usage 행 (두 styles/ 트리 byte-identical 미러 · additive).
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: easy-doc
plugins.desc: Easy-doc authoring — turn a technical file (or a topic) into a layperson-friendly sibling `<name>.easy.md`. Applies the canonical easy reference (hooks/easy-auto/styles/easy.<lang>.md, source-of-truth — not duplicated): the 7-element pattern (icon · name · alias · plain-line · analogy · ASCII · compare), the 4 ASCII structure templates (before-after · tree · side-by-side · structure-sketch), and the jargon→everyday translation checklist. Skill (natural-language trigger) + /easy-doc command. Ships one worked sample (samples/cache.easy.md). Authoring-only (markdown output, no executable hook logic); reads the input → applies the easy contract per document shape → writes the sibling `.easy.md`. Pairs with the `easy` skill (response style) — easy-doc is the FILE-output sibling. 0.2.0 — wraps the `hexa easy` builtin (scaffold → LLM slot-fill → lint gate; manual fallback when unsynced). 0.1.0 — initial.
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: easy-auto
plugins.desc: 0.4.0 (2026-06-06) ASCII 강제 강화 (2층위). (1) 주입 헤더 최상단에 front-load 된 ASCII 필수 mandate + 4종 템플릿(전후 →/트리 ├─└─/나란히 │/구조 [ ]──▶) inline skeleton + 1줄 self-check + 제외목록 — reference 본문에 묻혀 살리언스 낮던 ASCII 항목을 응답 직전 가장 먼저 보이게 끌어올림 (기존 body 그대로 아래 · additive). (2) 신규 Stop 이벤트 _easy_ascii_stop.hexa — transcript 마지막 assistant 메시지가 non-trivial(≥400자·코드/JSON 과반 아님)인데 fenced ``` 블록 안에 box-drawing 문자(│├└─┌┐┘→▶╲╱) 없으면 advisory systemMessage 출력. decision:block 절대 미사용(verdict-gate 선례 — 자율루프 trap 방지)·stop_hook_active true면 즉시 skip·미충족 precondition silent skip. sidecar @D s7 충족. 0.3.2 (2026-06-03) inject-only hook wrapper now ALWAYS exits 0. 0.3.1 (2026-06-01) hooks.json hexa-run wrapper now fails open — a compile/runtime error exits 0 (guard deny exit 2 preserved), so a transient "compile error" trailer no longer spams every command; pairs with install.hexa serial hook-precompile warming. SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit + PreCompact + PostCompact hook — auto-injects the `easy` (friendly) 7-element response style as additionalContext so the pattern is active from turn 0 without the user calling /easy. Reads ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/styles/easy.<lang>.md (env `EASY_LANG` override, default `ko`); falls back to easy.md (English base) when the lang variant is missing. UserPromptSubmit re-injects every turn so the style never fades; PreCompact + PostCompact survive auto-compaction. Implemented in hexa-lang (`_easy_auto.hexa`, invoked via `hexa run`). Pairs with the `easy` skill (manual /easy trigger remains — easy-auto is the default-on layer). `EASY_LANG` only SELECTS the style language (default `ko`) — not a disable switch. NO opt-out by design (commons @D g11 / sidecar @D s11); 0.1.2 removed the `EASY_LANG=off` suppress path. 0.2.0 — 한국어 substring 트리거 '설명'/'쉽게' 추가 (UserPromptSubmit 시 verb/noun/adverb 모든 어형 catch: '설명해'/'설명해줌'/'설명'/'설명서'/'쉽게'/'쉽게 알려줌' 등; 오탐 가능성 수용) + 발동 시 1줄 banner emit ('🎓 easy 모드 활성 — 7-요소 패턴 적용 …'). 기존 inject는 그대로 always-on (trigger gating 아님 — banner만 추가). 0.3.0 — 일반인+ASCII 강화: 5개 언어 styles/easy.<lang>.md 에 ASCII 구조 4종 템플릿(전후/트리/나란히/구조) + 일반인 gold(전문용어→생활어 BEFORE/AFTER) + 일반인-번역 체크리스트 + 측정 축 ascii-structure-template-usage 행 추가 (additive · 훅 로직 무변경).
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: easy-paper
plugins.desc: /easy-paper <slug-or-paper.md> — authors a layperson `.easy.paper.md` companion of a paper. Reads a PAPER/<slug>/ dir (per PAPER.tape roster) or a given paper .md, then emits `<slug>.easy.paper.md` with FOUR paper-specific sections: (1) 평이-초록 plain-language abstract, (2) ASCII figure sketches (the easy 4-template set: before-after · tree · side-by-side · structure), (3) 비유 섹션 analogy-driven method/finding, (4) "이 논문이 한 일" one-paragraph what-it-did summary — all under the easy 7-element pattern. Source-of-truth = easy-auto/styles/easy.<lang>.md (point + summarize, NOT duplicated). Sidecar to `paper` + `easy`; READ-ONLY on the source paper (never edits main.tex / PAPER.md / PAPER.tape / verdicts; a negative-result paper stays a negative result — no invented numbers). One worked sample bundled (sample-cost-routing.easy.paper.md). 0.2.0 — gates the finished companion through the deterministic `hexa easy lint` builtin (per-axis 측정 축 + PASS/FAIL; manual fallback when unsynced); scaffold not used (paper-specific 4-section output). 0.1.0 — initial.
plugins.author: dancinlab

plugins.name: research
plugins.desc: 0.2.5 (2026-06-04) fix: arxiv 429 rate-limit handling — `_arxiv.hexa` now captures the HTTP status (`curl -w "\n%{http_code}"`) and detects a rate-limit (HTTP 429 OR a literal `Rate exceeded.` body) explicitly, entering a backoff-retry loop (sleep 3s · 6s · 12s, honoring arXiv's ~3s min inter-request interval) before reporting failure. On persistent rate-limit it prints `research/arxiv: rate-limited by arXiv (HTTP 429) — retry shortly` and exits non-zero, instead of the previous misleading `no results` (which masked transient 429s as empty feeds). `no results` is now reserved for a genuine HTTP-200 empty feed; the success parse path is unchanged. Research-fetch tools — `/research:arxiv <query|id>` searches the official arXiv API or fetches by id (title · authors · abstract · pdf); `/research:yt <url-or-id>` extracts YouTube caption transcript via the InnerTube ANDROID client. Implemented in hexa-lang (`_arxiv.hexa` / `_yt.hexa`, invoked via `hexa run`); HTTP via curl, no API key. Error paths (network · parse · no-captions · bad-id) exit non-zero so callers can tell failure from a real result.

plugins.name: gh-stack
plugins.desc: 0.2.0 (2026-06-06) GROWS TEETH (guard-teeth-sweep @L5 · s7) — adds a DETERMINISTIC per-layer line-count gate `bin/gh_stack_lint.sh <layer-below> [head]`: sums `git diff --numstat <base>..HEAD` (added+deleted) and FAILs (exit 1) over the fixed 200-line cap, run before each `gh pr create --base <layer-below>`. Graceful skip (exit 0) when git absent / diff uncomputable; the 200 cap is fixed (no env opt-out · s11). Stacked-PR workflow skill — proposes `gh stack` commands (enabled repos) or the manual `gh pr create --base previous-layer` fallback. Encodes the <200-lines-per-layer · 1-concern governance.

plugins.desc: /paper <args> — arxiv-style LaTeX paper scaffolder (v0.12 — s3 portable-path fix: the help text for `verify-block` now shows `$HOME/.hx/bin/hexa` instead of a hardcoded `/Users/ghost/...` absolute, matching the `env_var("HOME")` idiom the runnable already uses). Verbs: list [--sync] · set <slug> · show [<slug>] · goal <text> · title <text> · ms <text> · done <match> · todo <text> · new <slug> · sample [<name>] [<dest>] · samples · monograph-init <slug> [N] · fill <letter> · fig <size> <prompt> <out.png> · compile [dir] · lint [dir] · companion {init|sync} · outline [dir] · pipeline ... · atoms <domain> · verify-block ... · bib add <id> · pr-roll <OWNER/REPO> <since> · arxiv-prep [<dir>] · help. v0.11 fixes (INBOX #112 from demiurge ANTIMATTER): (1) pr-roll — early reject for bare repo name + jq `\\#` escape so LaTeX `\#` survives; (2) atoms — LC_ALL=C around BSD awk + lowercase compare + matches `fn <name>(` dispatch lines; (3) arxiv-prep — resolves dir to absolute path before tar subshell. v0.10 PAPER.tape roster + per-paper PAPER.md/log.md unchanged.

plugins.name: imagine
plugins.desc: /imagine <prompt-file> <out.png> [-s size] [-b backend] [-m model] — generic AI image generator. Two backends out of the box: `fal` (queue+poll fal.ai, default — `secret get fal.api_key`, model = openai/gpt-image-2 firm-pinned default) and `openai` (sync /v1/images/generations — `secret get openai.api_key`, model = gpt-image-1). Canonical fal-style size tokens (`square_hd` / `landscape_16_9` / `portrait_16_9` / `square`) translate per-backend. Prompt always read from a file (provenance), payload JSON via mktemp (prompt never on argv). Backend pluggable — drop a new `_backends/<name>.hexa` to add one.

plugins.name: output-trim
plugins.desc: 0.1.5 (2026-06-01) hooks.json hexa-run wrapper now fails open — a compile/runtime error exits 0 (guard deny exit 2 preserved), so a transient "compile error" trailer no longer spams every command; pairs with install.hexa serial hook-precompile warming. PreToolUse(Bash) stdout trimmer — when a simple single Bash command would emit >8000 chars, transparently rewrite via `updatedInput` (emitted with `permissionDecision: allow` in the same hookSpecificOutput — REQUIRED, else Claude Code ignores the rewrite and stdout is never trimmed; the 0.1.3 fix) to pipe stdout through a minimal hexa-native kernel: consecutive-line dedup ([×N] counter) + per-line truncation to 200 chars. Small outputs <8000 chars pass verbatim. Skipped on any shell metacharacter so compound pipelines / redirects / heredocs / background jobs / command substitutions and other PreToolUse(Bash) rewrite hooks compose without conflict. Exit code preserved via `set -o pipefail`. Kernel chosen by benchmark on 120 real Bash-stdout samples ≥8000 chars — Pareto-dominates the TF-IDF salience + MinHash near-dup paragraph dedup approach of the original `wilson-output-trim`. 0.1.4 — dead retired-rule source citation in plugin.json replaced with the current no-opt-out rule (project.tape @D s11). NO opt-out by design.

plugins.name: subagent-route
plugins.desc: 0.1.1 (2026-06-01) hooks.json hexa-run wrapper now fails open — a compile/runtime error exits 0 (guard deny exit 2 preserved), so a transient "compile error" trailer no longer spams every command; pairs with install.hexa serial hook-precompile warming. [POC] PreToolUse(Task|Agent) observation hook + SessionStart observation-log snapshot, implemented in hexa-lang (`_subagent_route.hexa`, invoked via `hexa run`). v0.1.0 is observation-only — it does NOT deny, NOT rewrite. On every Task/Agent fire it dumps `tool_input` (key list + agent_type + prompt preview + isolation) to `~/.sidecar/subagent-route.log.jsonl` (capped 100 lines, jsonl format mirroring pool-route's route-log) and emits a non-blocking `additionalContext` advisory suggesting the equivalent `ssh <host> -- claude --print --no-tty -p '<prompt>'` rewrite. SessionStart event reads the last 5 observations back as additionalContext so the model sees recent subagent fires without recon. PoC purpose — probe the actual tool_input payload shape at runtime (Claude Code docs leave Agent/Task tool_input fields under-specified vs Bash), and probe the `additionalContext` UX before a real-rewrite v0.2.0. Always exits 0; advisory only.

plugins.name: worktree-gc
plugins.desc: 0.2.1 (2026-06-01) hooks.json hexa-run wrapper now fails open — a compile/runtime error exits 0 (guard deny exit 2 preserved), so a transient "compile error" trailer no longer spams every command; pairs with install.hexa serial hook-precompile warming. SessionStart hook that prunes merged-but-undeleted LINKED git worktrees in the cwd repo, implemented in hexa-lang (`_worktree_gc.hexa`, invoked via `hexa run`). Threshold gate (linked-count >= 3 OR disk avail < 20 GiB) keeps the common case (1-2 worktrees, ample disk) silent. Above threshold, fetches `gh pr list --state merged --limit 200` and considers a worktree only when its branch is in that merged set OR its HEAD commit truly landed on origin/main. 0.2.0 adds FOUR unconditional live-work guards so an active worktree is NEVER wiped mid-task: (a) dirty-tree (uncommitted changes → SKIP), (b) recent-mtime (HEAD commit or any file modified < 1h → SKIP), (c) cwd-in-use (a live process' cwd is in the worktree, via lsof → SKIP), (d) HEAD-ancestor real-merged check (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <wt-HEAD> origin/main`) — a vanished `origin/<branch>` ref alone is IGNORED so a reused branch name can't condemn fresh work. (e) Atomic prune: `git worktree remove` is the sole removal path; on failure NOTHING is deleted (no partial / manual rm). Open-PR worktrees are NEVER touched. gh unavailable / no merged PRs → short note + no action. Always exits 0 (non-blocking). NO opt-out by design.

plugins.name: sidecar-auto-sync
plugins.desc: 0.2.1 (2026-06-01) hooks.json hexa-run wrapper now fails open — a compile/runtime error exits 0 (guard deny exit 2 preserved), so a transient "compile error" trailer no longer spams every command; pairs with install.hexa serial hook-precompile warming. SessionStart hook that runs `sidecar sync` once per Claude Code session, implemented in hexa-lang (`_sidecar_auto_sync.hexa`, invoked via `hexa run`). Closes the gap between an upstream `git push` on origin/main and the local plugin cache — no more manual `sidecar sync` between sessions. Silent on success; brief stderr advisory on failure. Skipped silently only on a real precondition: the `sidecar` binary not on PATH (fresh machine without `hx install sidecar` yet). Adds ~1-2s to session startup (network pull + cache copy + installed_plugins.json patch). NO opt-out by design (project.tape @D s11) — no env var / config disable switch; uninstall the plugin for manual control.

plugins.name: s9-guard
plugins.desc: 0.1.1 (2026-06-01) hooks.json hexa-run wrapper now fails open — a compile/runtime error exits 0 (guard deny exit 2 preserved), so a transient "compile error" trailer no longer spams every command; pairs with install.hexa serial hook-precompile warming. PreToolUse(Bash) advisory hook for load-assessment commands (project.tape @D s9). Fires when a Bash command looks like a Mac load check — `uptime` (word) · `loadavg` / `vm.loadavg` (substring) · `ps -A` adjacency or `ps -Ao pcpu` · `top -l ` (macOS) / `top -b ` (Linux) · `getloadavg`. Emits non-blocking systemMessage reminding the agent that any conclusion drawn from raw load must EXCLUDE `claude` PIDs (claude sessions are exempt from local load attribution) and suggesting the canonical claude-excluded sum (`ps -Ao pcpu,comm | awk '$2 !~ /claude/ {s+=$1} END {print int(s)}'`). NEVER blocks — pure advisory. Implemented in hexa-lang (`_s9_guard.hexa`, invoked via `hexa run`). Ships per @D s7 (governance + enforcement together) — the @D s9 companion guard. NO opt-out by design.

plugins.name: askq-text
plugins.desc: 0.1.1 (2026-06-01) hooks.json hexa-run wrapper now fails open — a compile/runtime error exits 0 (guard deny exit 2 preserved), so a transient "compile error" trailer no longer spams every command; pairs with install.hexa serial hook-precompile warming. PreToolUse(AskUserQuestion) → plain-text chat redirect, in hexa-lang (`_askq_text.hexa`, via `hexa run`). AskUserQuestion renders an arrow-key option-tree box in the TUI; this host prefers plain CHAT — questions asked as ordinary text, answered conversationally. A PreToolUse hook cannot re-render the box as text (no transform API), so the hook DENIES the call with an instruction telling the model to re-emit the SAME question as plain text in its reply (state it in prose, list any options inline marking a recommendation, accept a free-form answer). A FORM redirect, NOT anti-punt — the model SHOULD still ask, just in chat rather than the box (distinct from the `bypass` skill, which is about NOT asking clearly-OK reversible work). Plan approval keeps ExitPlanMode and is NOT touched. Unconditional — the tool name IS the precondition, NO env-var / flag escape hatch (project.tape @D s11). NO opt-out by design.

plugins.name: lsp-rebuild
plugins.desc: 0.2.1 (2026-06-01) hooks.json hexa-run wrapper now fails open — a compile/runtime error exits 0 (guard deny exit 2 preserved), so a transient "compile error" trailer no longer spams every command; pairs with install.hexa serial hook-precompile warming. PostToolUse(Write|Edit) auto-rebuild for hexa-native LSP servers, in hexa-lang (`_lsp_rebuild.hexa`, via `hexa run`). When the agent edits an LSP grammar source matching `*/lsp/<lang>_lsp.hexa`, the prebuilt `~/.local/bin/<lang>-lsp-hexa` is stale (next LSP session would run the old grammar), so the hook rebuilds it in the BACKGROUND — `nohup env HEXA_MAC_BUILD_OK=1 hexa build <src> -o ~/.local/bin/<lang>-lsp-hexa` (detached `&` → PostToolUse returns immediately; output → ~/.sidecar/lsp-rebuild.log) — and emits a non-blocking advisory. Keeps the build artifact in lockstep with the canonical .hexa grammar SSOT so a grammar change auto-propagates without a manual rebuild. Rebuild-not-source-run because the hexa LSP stdio server needs the `read_stdin_n_c` FFI which only links into a COMPILED binary. Fires on the `*/lsp/*_lsp.hexa` pattern AND on hexa-lang's own LSP (`self/lsp.hexa` monolith + `self/lsp/*.hexa` submodules — NOT named `*_lsp.hexa`), rebuilt via its `tool/build_hexa_lsp.hexa` orchestrator → `<repo>/bin/hexa-lsp` (project.tape @D s11). Pairs with the `*-lsp` wiring plugins (hexa-lsp · kosmos-lsp · n6-lsp · hxc-lsp). NO opt-out by design.

plugins.name: step-by-step
plugins.desc: 0.15.0 — Step 1(Parse) RESOLVER-FIRST: `!`-exec's recommend-axes `resolve-mode <args>` (0.5.0) and OBEYS its two-line output (`mode: …[ ← inherited from recommend-default]` + `resolved: mode=.. axis=.. weights=.. source=…`) as authoritative — DETERMINISTIC resolver reads `~/.sidecar/recommend-default` + computes LOCKED precedence (explicit `auto:<axis>`/`<weights>`/`manual` > inherited FIXED axis for bare `auto`/no token > 4-axis 1:1:1:1 > MANUAL) IN CODE, so bare `/sbs auto` reliably inherits a standing FIXED axis (s7 teeth — was 100% model prose). Resolver unsynced/errors/empty → FALL BACK to in-context `# default mode:` directive (advisory · same SSOT). `CLI 파일읽기 ≠ 모델 파일읽기` 화해 1줄 added to both sbs.md + step-by-step.md; existing model-targeted '모델은 파일 읽지 말라' wording preserved. lockstep recommend-axes 0.5.0. /step-by-step (alias /sbs) — plan-first sequential runbook with TWO modes (auto · manual default · 0.5.0 2-mode redesign) + 0.6.0 자동 4축 QA after ship (functional·visible·conformance·regression · regression FAIL → auto-revert · 나머지 alert · SKIP=PASS-equivalent · 결과는 plan.md `## qa-results`). MANUAL (the DEFAULT) — chat-form disambiguation: ONE question per round in chat (NOT AskUserQuestion), each round framed with the easy-mode 7-element scaffold (icon · canonical name · friendly alias · plain-line · everyday analogy · ASCII sketch · option compare-table · one-line recommendation) and closed with `→ A · B · 또는 자유응답` (free-form answers explicitly OK). Repeat round-by-round until ambiguity = 0, THEN render a `🎯 합의된 결정셋 (N개)` ASCII tree of every accumulated decision and PAUSE — user types `go` to confirm or `Qn=<other>` to flip ONLY that one (re-render after each flip). On `go`, write `drafts/<slug>-plan.md` (gitignored; frontmatter slug/mode/auto-weights/created + task brief + locked decisions + next-action checklist ending with a ship line + completion criteria) and LAUNCH A BACKGROUND AGENT (general-purpose, run_in_background=true) with a self-contained prompt — the agent runs end-to-end including ship + auto-QA 4축, no further user input needed; user can leave. AUTO — same chat-form scaffold rendered, but each question is AUTO-PICKED by the 4-axis weighted average instead of waiting for the user: 완성도 (complete · robust + edge-case coverage) + 단순 (simple · Occam) + 안전 (safe · blast radius minimized) + 표준 (std · fits the sidecar pattern), default 1:1:1:1, inline override `/sbs auto:safety <task>` (single-axis force) or `/sbs auto:complete=2,simple=3 <task>` (explicit weights). AUTO still pauses at the agreement screen so auto-picks get a user pre-commit checkpoint. Mid-run new ambiguity also opens a chat round + re-renders the agreement screen. Mode = FIRST arg token `auto`[:`<axis-or-weights>`] | `manual` (default manual). `legacy-manual` = the old per-step pause behavior — 1-version deprecation banner, use plain `manual` going forward. `go` is NOT a mode (use `/go` to continue the paused flow). ALL modes halt on a step failure (failing step + verbatim error + un-run tail) and pause before a genuinely irreversible / destructive / outward-facing step (confirm-then-resume, same bar as the bypass self-check). 0.6.0 auto-QA 4축 (handoff agent ship 직후 자동 실행): functional (새 endpoint/verb 응답) · visible (URL/path/surface 노출) · conformance (locked decision ↔ 코드 1:1) · regression (기존 surface 미손상). Hybrid fail 정책 — regression FAIL만 auto-revert (`git revert <SHA> && git push && sidecar sync`) + banner, 나머지 3축은 ship 유지 + plan.md `## qa-deferred` append + banner. ALL PASS/SKIP → banner 없이 plan.md `## qa-results`에 ✓ 라인만 append. 0.7.0 — ship+QA 직후 자동 HANDOFF.md 9-section 인계 doc (PR 매트릭스 · SSOT 파일 인덱스 · 새 API surface · 컴포넌트 트리 · env 변수 · 다음 우선순위 · 한계+guard · memory 인덱스 · 한 줄 시작 가이드; `memory/project_<slug>_handoff.md` 미러 · plan에 handoff verb 면 end-user dossier bundle 도). 0.8.0 — plan.md frontmatter `status: active` stamp 규약 + `## locked decisions` 불릿 기계가독 contract 확장 `- @L<n> (<axis>): <option> · assert:<grep|file|verdict> <arg>` (grep <pat>·`!pat`=부재 / file <path>·존재 / verdict <slug>/<id>·`.verdicts/` non-empty). 신규 `plan-guard` 플러그인이 이 marker 를 sub-agent 프롬프트에 verbatim 주입 + ship 시 `plan-lint` 검증; `@L` 없는 기존 plan.md 는 skip (후방호환). 0.8.1 — plan 라이프사이클 명시: write 시 frontmatter `status: active` stamp 必 (정확히 1개만 active), closure 시 `status: done`(폐기 시 `abandoned`)로 flip — plan-guard 활성추적(@L6)이 stale plan 의 @L 을 잘못 강제하지 않게 함. 0.9.0 — chat-form 7-element 라운드 scaffold 를 `hexa easy` 빌트인에 배선(easy-doc·easy-paper 와 동일 패턴): `hexa easy scaffold` 가 결정적 7-슬롯 골격 · LLM 이 창의 슬롯만 채움 · `hexa easy lint` 가 라운드 prose 품질의 advisory 게이트(disambiguation/auto-pick 로직은 빌트인 독립 · 항상 실행). SSOT = hooks/easy-auto/styles/easy.<lang>.md (중복 금지) · toolchain 미동기 시 self-check graceful fallback. 0.10.0 — Step 0.9 인계가 **ad-hoc HANDOFF.md 작성을 폐지** (commons @D g36 · g59 · g60 · s16: handoff 는 단일 `sidecar handoff` 레지스트리로, scattered .md / per-repo INBOX 금지). 대체 carrier 둘: (a) intra-repo 9-section dossier → `drafts/<slug>-plan.md` 의 `## handoff` 섹션 append (gitignored · s16), (b) cross-repo follow-up → `sidecar handoff add <repo>` 레지스트리. memory mirror = `MEMORY.md` 인덱스 한 줄 (별도 pointer 파일 폐지). 신규 `handoff-guard` 플러그인이 root/`domains/HANDOFF.md` 작성을 PreToolUse hard-deny → 재발 차단 (s7 — 규칙+enforcement 동반; `inbox/` 는 atlas-submission 등으로 과적재된 이름이라 guard 제외). 0.11.0 — Step 0 parse 가 recommend-axes 기본값을 상속 (명시 mode token 없을 때 `~/.sidecar/recommend-default` 매핑: present→MANUAL · auto→AUTO 1:1:1:1 · complete|simple|safe|std→해당 축 forced; 우선순위 EXPLICIT > recommend-default > MANUAL). 0.12.0 — 상속을 **파일 읽기 → in-context 디렉티브 준수**로 전환 (s7 신뢰성 fix): recommend-axes 훅이 매 턴 주입하는 `# default mode:` 디렉티브가 단일 SSOT — sbs 는 더 이상 `~/.sidecar/recommend-default` 를 별도로 읽지 않고 (모델이 자주 건너뛰던 skippable step 제거) 이미 컨텍스트에 있는 디렉티브를 OBEY: `# default mode: AUTO …`→AUTO 4-axis 1:1:1:1 · `# default mode: FIXED <axis> …`→AUTO 해당 단일 axis forced (auto-proceed · agreement 1회) · 디렉티브 부재(present)→MANUAL. 우선순위 EXPLICIT arg token > in-context 디렉티브 > MANUAL fallback. recommend-axes 0.4.0 의 AUTO/FIXED 디렉티브가 /sbs mode 도 관장한다는 절을 실어 enforcement 동반 (s7). 0.13.0 — disambiguation 보증 강화 (stepwise/ambiguity→0 audit): Step 0.5 re-scan→zero 루프를 advisory → **non-skippable hard gate** 격상 (ambiguity > 0 인 채 agreement 진입 금지 · AUTO short-circuit 불가 · 유일 exit = explicit zero re-scan) · up-front 전체 enumeration MANDATORY 명시 · no-fabrication 보증 MANUAL → **BOTH 모드** 확장 (AUTO 는 enumerate 된 옵션만 pick · missing FACT 는 invent 말고 agreement 에 surface) · Step 0.6 agreement 에 zero-gate precondition 추가. sbs.md alias 도 요약 수준 동일 보증 (parity). doc-only (NO hexa). 0.14.0 — BARE `auto` 토큰(정확히 `auto`, `:axis`/`:weights` 없음)이 standing FIXED recommend-default axis 를 상속 (예전엔 항상 4-axis 1:1:1:1): in-context `# default mode: FIXED <axis>` 디렉티브가 있으면 그 단일 axis forced(나머지 셋 weight 0)로 AUTO · `← inherited from recommend-default` 노트 (no-token 상속과 동일 wording) · 디렉티브 AUTO/present/absent 면 4-axis 1:1:1:1 유지. 명시 `auto:<axis>`/`auto:<weights>` 는 inherited FIXED axis 보다 우선 (axis 우선순위: explicit auto:<axis> > inherited FIXED axis (bare auto / no token) > 4-axis 1:1:1:1). step-by-step.md + sbs.md mode-parse prose lockstep · MANUAL/agreement/handoff 불변 · doc-only (NO hexa).

plugins.name: deck
plugins.desc: /deck <domain> <slug> '<spec-json>' — 🍞 도메인 input deck 빵틀 generator. Thin wrapper around `hexa-lang stdlib/deck/gen.hexa`. v0.2 — s3 portable-path fix: the Step-1 runnable now invokes `hexa run $HOME/.hx/install/hexa-lang/stdlib/deck/gen.hexa …` instead of a hardcoded `/Users/ghost/...` absolute (pool-route 0.15.0 ships the companion `stdlib/deck/gen.hexa` LOCAL pin so the now-`/Users/`-free command still stays local). RTSC QE el-ph first impl (4 files emit: vc-relax.in · scf.in · ph.in · run.sh; spec keys = anchor · press · q_grid · sscha? · soc?; PSL 1.0.0 pseudo auto-branch on `soc` flag). Output dir = exports/<domain>/decks/<slug>/. chem/chip/bio/nuclear/material stub (TODO — first RTSC impl confirms pattern, then graduation = add emit_<domain>() in stdlib/deck/gen.hexa + manifest stub→full flip). plugins.name: walkie
plugins.desc: 📻 /walkie — session-to-session walkie-talkie over a UNIX domain socket, NO MCP (sidecar @D s15). Two Claude Code TUI sessions exchange one-line JSON messages: the CALL side is a CLI one-liner (`socat - UNIX-CONNECT:<peer>.sock`, fallback `nc -U <path>`); the receive side is the agent arming a persistent Monitor — `on` directly on `socat UNIX-LISTEN:<self>.sock,fork -`, OR, when the `walkie-arm` hook's capture daemon owns the socket and durably captures to `<self>.inbox.log`, on `tail -f <self>.inbox.log` (phase-2 coexistence — `on` auto-retargets) — so each received line surfaces as a chat task-notification. Local mailbox + roster under `~/.sidecar/walkie/` (roster.json maps handle -> socket path + sid + ts) so pool-route keeps it LOCAL. Radio verbs — `on` (listen: upsert self + print the Monitor command, retargeting to the inbox log when walkie-arm is present) · `call <handle> <text...>` (direct; roster-miss falls back to the default `<handle>.sock` path so a peer that armed via `arm` — bind-only, unregistered — is still reachable, graceful peer-offline hint when not live) · `all-call <text...>` (every peer) · `scan` (roster table, alive marked via `test -S`, dead rows flagged not deleted) · `handle <name>` · `arm [<handle>]` (print the exact persistent-Monitor listen command for self or a named peer so a parent can paste it into a sub-agent prompt — main->sub steer) · bare `/walkie` (status). OLD verbs (listen/send/broadcast/who/nick) still dispatch as silent aliases. NL triggers via the skill — '무전' · '워키토키' · '세션끼리 통신' · '옆 세션에 보내' · 'call session' · 'socket message' · 'inter-session' · 'steer sub-agent'.

plugins.name: walkie-arm
plugins.desc: 0.2.1 (2026-06-03) inject-only hook wrapper now ALWAYS exits 0 — a transient toolchain rebuild (hexa.real returning compile-error rc=2 mid-`sidecar sync`) can no longer block prompt submission for this advisory/inject hook (it never denies — only emits additionalContext); genuine guards keep their exit-2 deny. 0.2.0 (2026-06-02) phase-4 SUB-AGENT AUTO-ARM-ON-SPAWN — a new PreToolUse(Task|Agent) `inject` verb makes EVERY spawned sub-agent steerable mid-flight over walkie WITHOUT the operator pasting `/walkie arm` output into the spawn prompt. A sub-agent is NOT a session, so the SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hooks never fire for it; this verb (plan-guard inject pattern — additionalContext only, never `updatedInput`, never a deny) mints a UNIQUE child handle per spawn (`sub-<frag>-<seq>`; frag from the Task subagent_type/description sanitized to [a-z0-9-], seq from a persisted `~/.sidecar/walkie/seq` counter), registers it into roster.json via `_register_self` (so the main session sees it via `/walkie scan`), spawns the SAME detached capture daemon for the child socket (steers sent between the sub's polls are durably captured to `<child>.inbox.log`), and emits an additionalContext block telling the sub it is handle `<child>` + the canonical Monitor-arm / offset-drain listen command + how to ack via `/walkie call <parent>`. Idempotent — skips (empty output) when the spawn prompt already contains the `📻 walkie auto-arm` marker (re-spawn / nested). s11 precondition-gated (self handle set + socat|nc present), else silent exit 0 — NO opt-out switch. 📻 SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit hook — phase-2 AUTO-RECEIVE for the `walkie` plugin, NO MCP (sidecar @D s15). A UNIX socket is a connection not a queue, so phase-1 `/walkie on` drops every message that arrives while no one is bound. walkie-arm closes the gap: on SessionStart it upserts self into `~/.sidecar/walkie/roster.json` and spawns a DETACHED capture daemon (`socat UNIX-LISTEN:<self>.sock,fork OPEN:<self>.inbox.log,append,create`, fallback `nc -lkU`; setsid→nohup) that OWNS the socket and appends every received line to `<self>.inbox.log` — idempotent via a `<self>.daemon.pid` pidfile + pgrep guard, stale socket `rm -f` before bind. On SessionStart + every UserPromptSubmit it drains `<self>.inbox.log` from the byte offset in `<self>.offset`, emits new lines as additionalContext (`📨 from X: ...`, capped ~20 with an overflow summary), and advances the offset (resets to 0 on truncation/rotation). Self handle from `~/.sidecar/walkie/self` (shared SSOT with the `walkie` command plugin). hexa-lang (`_walkie_arm.hexa`). Pairs with `walkie` 0.3.0 whose `on` retargets to `tail -f <self>.inbox.log` when the daemon owns the socket.

plugins.name: walkie-mcp
plugins.desc: 0.1.4 (2026-06-02) broker no longer gates on a walkie handle. plugin.json declares the http MCP url (127.0.0.1:7717) UNCONDITIONALLY so the host always tries to connect — but launcher AND server both `exit 0` when no `~/.sidecar/walkie/self` handle was set (the common case), leaving `/mcp` RED (connection refused). Fix: the broker now LISTENS regardless of the handle (gate is node-present only, s11) and the inbox tail resolves the self handle LAZILY per 1s tick — a handle set AFTER startup activates idle-push with NO restart. Verified: with no handle, `initialize` over http succeeds; then setting a handle + writing an inbox line emits the channel notification live. 0.1.3 (2026-06-01) hooks.json hexa-run wrapper now fails open — a compile/runtime error exits 0 (guard deny exit 2 preserved), so a transient "compile error" trailer no longer spams every command; pairs with install.hexa serial hook-precompile warming. 📻 walkie phase-3 IDLE-PUSH — an HTTP/SSE-transport MCP channels server (sidecar @D s15 1.8 allows HTTP/SSE MCP; STDIO MCP stays forbidden). walkie(0.3.0) + walkie-arm(0.1.1) capture inbound session-to-session lines into `~/.sidecar/walkie/<self>.inbox.log`, but an idle session only drains them on its NEXT turn (poll). This plugin closes that gap: a single local Node broker (Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1:7717) tails `<self>.inbox.log` from a dedicated `<self>.mcp.offset` (separate from walkie-arm's `.offset` so the two never contend) and, per new JSON line `{from,text,ts}`, emits an MCP channel notification `method:notifications/claude/channel` `params:{content:"📨 from <handle>: <text>"}` — which Claude Code PUSHES into the live-but-idle session (no turn needed). The server declares the `experimental["claude/channel"]` capability the host requires; plugin.json exposes it as a `channels` entry + an http url-based `mcpServers` entry (NOT stdio command-based → lint passes). receive-PUSH only — send stays the existing `/walkie call` socket path (no re-implementation). SessionStart fires a detached daemon-launcher (`_walkie_mcp_up.hexa`; pidfile + pgrep guard, walkie-arm pattern; on first run `npm install --omit=dev @modelcontextprotocol/sdk` into the plugin dir if node_modules absent — node_modules never committed). sidecar's FIRST non-hexa (Node) executable. IDLE-PUSH requires Claude Code launched with `--dangerously-load-development-channels walkie-mcp` (or `--channels walkie-mcp` once GA) AND a first-party provider (Bedrock/Vertex skip) — experimental research-preview. NO opt-out switch (s11) — gates only on the real precondition node-present (NOT the handle), else graceful exit 0. NO absolute paths ($HOME/$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT only). 0.1.2 — STATEFUL multi-session transport fix: per-session Server+transport keyed by the SDK session id (was a single shared Server re-connect()ed per request, which orphaned a prior client's long-lived push SSE stream and surfaced host-side as 'socket connection closed unexpectedly' mid-turn); channel emits now fan out to EVERY connected session.

plugins.name: walkie-hexa
plugins.desc: 0.1.2 (2026-06-03) inject-only hook wrapper now ALWAYS exits 0 — a transient toolchain rebuild (hexa.real returning compile-error rc=2 mid-`sidecar sync`) can no longer block prompt submission for this advisory/inject hook (it never denies — only emits additionalContext); genuine guards keep their exit-2 deny. 0.1.1 (2026-06-01) hooks.json hexa-run wrapper now fails open — a compile/runtime error exits 0 (guard deny exit 2 preserved), so a transient "compile error" trailer no longer spams every command; pairs with install.hexa serial hook-precompile warming. 📡 SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit hook — the EMIT/sender side of the walkie family for hexa-lang releases (NO MCP, sidecar @D s15). Watches `$HOME/core/hexa-lang` git HEAD: on every SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit it reads `git -C $HOME/core/hexa-lang rev-parse --short HEAD` and, when the sha DIFFERS from the last-broadcast one in `~/.sidecar/walkie/hexa-lang.last-sha`, auto-broadcasts a one-line `📡 hexa-lang <short-sha>: <commit subject>` to EVERY live peer via the walkie all-call roster loop (verbatim from `/walkie all-call` — resolve each handle's sock from `~/.sidecar/walkie/roster.json`, build a `{from,text,ts}` JSON line, send via `socat - UNIX-CONNECT:<sock>` else `nc -U <sock>`, skip self, skip offline peers). Receiving is ALREADY handled by walkie-arm (capture daemon) + walkie-mcp (idle-push) — this plugin ONLY emits, never re-implements receive. Per-sha atomic `mkdir ~/.sidecar/walkie/.hexa-lang-lock-<sha>` lock → exactly ONE session fires per new sha even under concurrent ticks (the loser just records the sha). FIRST-SEEN (no last-sha file) records the current sha SILENTLY (not an update). Missing repo (`test -e <repo>/.git`) / unset self handle (`~/.sidecar/walkie/self`) / git failure → graceful exit 0. Never reads stdin (hexa fake-stdin trap — env + files + exec only; no self-path re-spawn). NO opt-out switch (s11) — gates only on real preconditions (hexa-lang/.git present + self handle set), else silent exit 0. hexa-lang (`_walkie_hexa.hexa tick`, via `hexa run`). NO absolute paths ($HOME/$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT only).

plugins.name: celebrate
plugins.desc: 0.1.3 (2026-06-01) hooks.json hexa-run wrapper now fails open — a compile/runtime error exits 0 (guard deny exit 2 preserved), so a transient "compile error" trailer no longer spams every command; pairs with install.hexa serial hook-precompile warming. 🎆 Stop hook that fires a fireworks celebration when the ACTIVE /domain's progress crosses to 100% (a 'novel goal' reached). On every turn-end it resolves the active domain (same convention as the `domain` skill — git repo root + `$HOME/.claude/domain-active.tsv` active pointer, else project basename; snapshot path via the repo's `DOMAINS.tape` roster) and counts `- [ ]`/`- [x]` milestones in the active DOMAIN.md (done/total; 100% = total>0 && done==total). It keeps the last-seen percent per domain in `$HOME/.sidecar/celebrate/<domain-key>.seen` and fires ONLY on the crossing (prev <100 → now =100), then records 100 so it never re-fires while it stays at 100; if it drops below 100 and re-reaches, it celebrates again (natural). On the crossing the hook (1) emits a multi-line ASCII fireworks burst + '🎆 <DOMAIN> @goal 100% 달성!' via the top-level `systemMessage` field into the chat (0.1.2 — Stop hooks do NOT support hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext), (2) rings the terminal bell (`printf '\a'`). HARD CONSTRAINT: the Claude Code TUI canvas is owned by Ink, so this hook NEVER writes ANSI/animation to /dev/tty (that would corrupt the screen) — the animation lives ONLY in the spawned separate window; the in-stream ASCII burst is static text. Non-macOS → skips (3), keeps (1)(2). UNCONDITIONAL (commons @D s11 — no env-var/flag/config escape hatch): the ONLY gates are real preconditions — an active domain exists AND has ≥1 milestone AND progress just crossed 100; no active domain / 0 milestones / not crossing → silent exit 0. hexa-lang (`_celebrate.hexa` + `_fireworks.hexa`, via `hexa run`); reads stdin via `exec("cat")` (avoids the hexa fake-FILE segfault), checks path existence via shell `test -e`, portable `$HOME`/`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` paths only.

plugins.name: agentmemory
plugins.desc: 0.1.0 (2026-06-02) persistent cross-session AGENT MEMORY — capture hook half of the agentmemory family (ported from rohitg00/agentmemory, Apache-2.0; AGENT CONTRACT only — NO Rust iii-engine / REST API / viewer / benchmark harness). SessionStart + PostToolUse(Write|Edit|MultiEdit|Bash) + PreCompact hook in hexa-lang (`_agentmemory_capture.hexa`, via `hexa run`; @D g1 hexa-native-first). THREE phases: (1) SessionStart injects the server-written recall snapshot for THIS project ($HOME/.sidecar/agentmemory/recall/<cwd-hash>.txt) as additionalContext, so a fresh session opens with the top-N relevant memories already in context — no snapshot → silent no-op; (2) PostToolUse captures ONE salient observation (file write/edit or command) into the working-memory capture queue ($HOME/.sidecar/agentmemory/queue/capture.jsonl) — a single JSON-line append, no DB, never blocks the tool call; (3) PreCompact drops a flush marker so the MCP server (agentmemory-mcp) rolls working→episodic (the upstream sleep-consolidation entry point). The 4-tier store SSOT schema (working · episodic · semantic · procedural + sessions + links) ships at store/schema.sql, applied on first use by the MCP server against $HOME/.sidecar/agentmemory/mem.db (s16 runtime state OUTSIDE the repo · s3 portable paths — $HOME/$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT only). ADVISORY · FAIL-OPEN — every path exits 0 on error, the deny exit-2 is never used (it nudges/queues, never blocks). NO opt-out switch (s11) — gates only on the salient-tool precondition. Pairs with agentmemory-mcp (MCP tool server) + memory (/memory command).

plugins.name: agentmemory-mcp
plugins.desc: 0.3.1 (2026-06-03) FIX (first-session MCP '✘ failed') — the host now launches the STDIO server via a SYNC launch wrapper (`bin/_agentmemory_mcp_launch.sh`) that ensures `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` is vendored BEFORE `exec`ing the server, closing the race where the host's immediate session-start launch beat the up-script's DETACHED `npm install` (first session after `sidecar sync` rebuilt the cache → node_modules absent → SDK import fail → panel `failed` until next session). Warm cache → instant exec; cold → ~7s sync install then serve (within the host MCP init timeout), up-script detached pre-warm still parallel. node_modules STILL never committed (s3 · s11 · fail-open). 0.3.0 (2026-06-02) adds the deferred VECTOR-EMBEDDING stream as the 4th RRF input in `memory_smart_search` — dense cosine similarity over an OPTIONAL embedding backend (`@xenova/transformers` BGE-small, an optionalDependency). New `vectors` table (L2-normalized Float32 BLOBs), embeddings computed best-effort on `memory_save` + backfillable via the NEW `memory_reindex` tool. GRACEFUL · regression-safe (@L4): backend absent → vector stream empty → smart-search fuses the same 3 streams as 0.2.0 byte-for-byte (s11 — gate is the real precondition, no opt-out). Enable: `npm i @xenova/transformers` in server dir, then `memory_reindex`. 0.2.0 (2026-06-02) `memory_smart_search` now does REAL hybrid relevance — three independent ranking streams fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF_K=60): BM25-lite keyword (title-weighted term overlap) + recency (ts desc) + graph-link (ids linked via the `links` table to the top keyword hits). Returns `{mode:hybrid, fusion, deferred, results:[{id,tier,title,score,…}]}`; an optional `project` filter scopes the pool. The vector-embedding stream is a documented FOLLOW-UP (@L4 · deferred) — a drop-in 4th RRF stream, no signature change. 0.1.0 (2026-06-02) the MCP-tool-server half of the agentmemory family — the FIRST permitted MCP server after the s15 STDIO-MCP ban was retired (PR #382). Ported from rohitg00/agentmemory (Apache-2.0; AGENT MCP CONTRACT only — NO Rust iii-engine / REST API / viewer / benchmark harness). Mirrors the walkie-mcp precedent: a hook plugin bundling a Node MCP server (`server/agentmemory-mcp-server.mjs`) + a hexa up-script (`bin/_agentmemory_mcp_up.hexa`, via `hexa run`). Exposes SIX core memory tools over STDIO transport against the 4-tier SQLite store at `$HOME/.sidecar/agentmemory/mem.db` (schema = PR1 `store/schema.sql` SSOT, bundled byte-identical at `server/schema.sql`, applied on first use): `memory_save` (save an insight/decision/fact into a chosen tier — working|episodic|semantic|procedural, default semantic), `memory_recall` (keyword recall across all 4 tiers, recency-ordered, full|compact), `memory_smart_search` (hybrid relevance — BM25-lite + recency + graph-link RRF fusion, RRF_K=60; vector stream deferred · @L4), `memory_sessions` (list recent sessions + summaries), `memory_forget` (delete a memory by id across tiers + its graph links), `memory_context` (compact top-N project snapshot + writes the SessionStart recall file the capture hook injects). On every tool call it lazily drains the PR1 capture queue (`$HOME/.sidecar/agentmemory/queue/capture.jsonl`) into the `working` tier. STORE = `node:sqlite` (built into Node >= 22.5 — no native build, no extra dep). The up-script's ONLY job is an on-demand DETACHED `npm install --omit=dev @modelcontextprotocol/sdk` on first run (node_modules NEVER committed); the STDIO server itself is launched by the HOST per the `mcpServers` command config (the host owns its lifecycle — a dedicated child process, so NO stdio collide with hexa hooks). plugin.json registers a command-based `mcpServers` entry (now permitted — s15 retired). FAIL-OPEN — the up-script + server both `exit 0` on any error, never blocking SessionStart. NO opt-out switch (s11) — gates only on real preconditions (node/npm present, sdk absent). NO absolute paths ($HOME / $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT only · s3). Pairs with agentmemory (capture hook) + memory (/memory command).

plugins.name: memory
plugins.desc: 0.3.0 (2026-06-02) `search` reaches PARITY with the MCP server — FOUR RRF streams (BM25-lite + recency + graph-link + dense vector-embedding), closing the graph-link gap AND the deferred vector tier (@L4). Vector stream uses OPTIONAL `@xenova/transformers` (optionalDependencies in the new commands/memory/package.json); `save` embeds best-effort + NEW `reindex [--limit N]` backfills. GRACEFUL: no backend → same RRF as before; `npm i @xenova/transformers` in commands/memory/ to enable. Reads the same `vectors` table the MCP server populates. 0.2.0 (2026-06-02) adds the `import <file>` verb — fold PRIOR history into the store: a .jsonl file imports per-line objects ({content|text,title,tier,concepts,type} → its tier, or a raw capture obs {title,file,session_id} → working); any other text file (e.g. a MEMORY.md) imports each markdown bullet / `[slug](path) — desc` index line as a semantic note. Idempotent via a content-fingerprint row id (re-import skips dups). /memory — persistent cross-session AGENT MEMORY CLI over the agentmemory 4-tier SQLite store ($HOME/.sidecar/agentmemory/mem.db · shared with the agentmemory capture hook + agentmemory-mcp MCP server). The command half of the agentmemory family (ported from rohitg00/agentmemory, Apache-2.0; AGENT CONTRACT only — NO Rust iii-engine / REST API / viewer / benchmark harness). Implemented as a Node CLI (`bin/memory.mjs`) over node:sqlite (built into Node >= 22.5 — no extra dep), invoked from the slash command via the cached-bin resolve pattern. VERBS: bare/`status` (tier counts working·episodic·semantic·procedural + session count + store path) · `save <text> [--tier working|episodic|semantic|procedural] [--title T] [--concepts a,b] [--type fact|pattern|preference|architecture|bug|workflow]` (default tier semantic) · `recall <query>` (cross-tier keyword recall, recency-ordered) · `search <query>` (HYBRID RRF relevance — BM25-lite keyword + recency + graph-link Reciprocal Rank Fusion, the same algorithm as the MCP server's memory_smart_search; vector-embedding stream deferred · @L4) · `sessions` (recent sessions with project·status·obs-count) · `forget <id>` (delete a memory by id across all tiers + its graph links) · `consolidate` (the upstream SLEEP-CONSOLIDATION pipeline: working→episodic [roll a session's salient observations into one summary + drop the folded working rows] → episodic→semantic [distill a concept recurring across >=2 episodic sessions into a durable semantic pattern] → semantic→procedural [promote a multi-step semantic note to a reusable how-to]; also auto-fired on PreCompact via the capture hook's flush marker) · `import <file>` (fold prior MEMORY.md / transcript JSONL history into the store, idempotent). Verified end-to-end: the full working→episodic→semantic→procedural cascade promotes across all four tiers; import folds both .jsonl and MEMORY.md with dedup. s16 runtime state OUTSIDE the repo · s3 portable paths. Pairs with agentmemory (capture hook) + agentmemory-mcp (MCP tool server).

plugins.name: project-setup
plugins.desc: Project configuration and setup tools including CLAUDE.md creation and maintenance with ground truth validation. The maintain flow preserves existing references and information by default - removal requires cross-verification proving the content false or obsolete (else: keep, extract to docs/, or ask the user) - and surfaces every single drift to the user via AskUserQuestion before applying any change (no batch-auto-fix, default on unanswered = leave unchanged). Includes a Phase 4b internal-duplication detection pass: file paths, pointers, and external resources are counted across the document; reference outliers (one path appearing N>1 times while peers appear once), conceptual restatements, and weak-justification duplicates (e.g., 'scannability' for jumping readers) are surfaced as per-drift questions with all N occurrences, peer-group comparison, and concrete merge/keep/cross-reference/extract options. Dedup merges are treated as deletions and require explicit per-item approval. Enforces a hard 40,000-character cap on CLAUDE.md (Claude Code performance warning threshold) by extracting bloated sections to docs/ via thin pointers. The project-structure section is required to document the EVERGREEN shape (top-level layout + repeating structural patterns + role per category), not an exhaustive file-by-file tree; file-by-file annotation is justified only where names alone are ambiguous, where the file is a key entry point, or to disambiguate siblings. Exhaustive file-by-file trees in existing CLAUDE.md files are flagged as Medium consolidation candidates (high decay risk, tokens without evergreen value) and surfaced as per-finding questions (consolidate / extract to docs/ / keep / skip), never collapsed autonomously. Generated CLAUDE.md files always include a canonical Working Principles section with 5 principles (4 inspired by upstream agentic-coding meta-rules: Think Before Coding, Simplicity First, Surgical Changes, Goal-Driven Execution; plus the locally authored Centralize Shared Logic for DRY / Single Source of Truth across external calls and cross-cutting concerns). Each of principles 1-4 ships with 3 inline sub-bullets covering the deeper meta-rules (root-cause analysis, evergreen tests, surgical diffs) so the block is self-contained and never linked out. The create/maintain flows auto-detect .deep-dive/ output and offer to ingest it as the technical-reference backbone.

plugins.name: overnight-review-panel-blocked-reviewer-reads-as-clean
plugins.desc: Companion safety pattern: in an unattended overnight review panel, a reviewer that couldn't see the code reads as a CLEAN one — usually because the code-review subagent lacks a Bash tool, so when told to `gh pr diff`/checkout a PR it returns a BLOCKED report (or reviews main, which predates the PR). Pre-generate per-base diffs + materialize worktrees + hand explicit paths, and treat BLOCKED as not-clean. Overnight specialization of the general skill code-reviewer-subagent-no-bash-blocked-on-pr-diff.
plugins.author: wan-huiyan

plugins.name: overnight-multi-issue-implementation
plugins.desc: Overnight autonomous workflow that takes a cluster of related GitHub issues (typically a P1 review-panel finding set) and ships them to merged stacked PRs by morning. Builds on subagent-driven-development with overnight-specific discipline: stacked PRs (so PR2 doesn't wait on a human PR1-merge mid-night), pre-flight tracker-id audit (concurrent sessions on main steal IDs), final PR-level code review before proposing merge, review findings preserved as PR comments before squash. Sister to overnight-review-client-delivery and overnight-insight-discovery.
plugins.author: wan-huiyan

plugins.name: large-redesign-parallel-branch-collision-audit
plugins.desc: Pre-flight audit before starting a large multi-PR redesign that rewrites shared files. Catches the failure mode where a long-running parallel feature branch (e.g. client-variant, staging, whitelabel) has unmerged commits touching the same files the redesign is about to rewrite — so they end up stranded with head-on conflicts that can't be cleanly cherry-picked. Sister to pre-merge-client-variant-regression-audit (audits a variant branch BEING merged into main; this audits BEFORE main diverges from a variant) and parallel-pr-scope-overlap-tiebreaker-delta-check (two simultaneous PRs vs. one redesign on main + WIP elsewhere). Companion to overnight-multi-issue-implementation for the file-collision dimension that the existing tracker-id audit doesn't cover.
plugins.author: wan-huiyan

plugins.name: subagent-review-tier-calibration-for-overnight-pr-chains
plugins.desc: Calibrate review intensity per-PR (Tier 1 two-stage / Tier 2 combined single-agent / Tier 3 bash-only verification) when orchestrating a long chain (10+ PRs) of independent tasks overnight from a single implementation plan. Specializes subagent-driven-development's review step for throughput-tuned chains: prescribes three tiers, a decision rubric, and a concrete bash-verification recipe for low-risk visual-restyle PRs. Sister to subagent-driven-development (master pattern; this specializes the review step) and overnight-multi-issue-implementation (different shape: stacked PRs from issues vs. independent PRs from plan). Companion to large-redesign-parallel-branch-collision-audit (pre-flight before STARTING a chain).
plugins.author: wan-huiyan

plugins.name: schedule-poll-orchestrator-pattern
plugins.desc: Fire-ASAP orchestrator pattern for multi-track autonomous overnight workflows on scheduled triggers — a self-rescheduling poll loop that consolidates the moment all tracks report complete, and survives a 12-20h session end. Companion safety pattern.

plugins.name: ecosystem
plugins.desc: Observability substrate for Claude Code. Provides the shared $ONLOOKER_DIR storage root (default $HOME/.onlooker), canonical schema-validated event emission, session and tool tracking hooks, and prompt rules. Required by all other Onlooker plugins.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: archivist
plugins.desc: Structured session memory across context truncation: extracts decisions, dead ends, and open questions on PreCompact and reinjects the most important items at SessionStart. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: cartographer
plugins.desc: Proactive periodic auditor of the persistent instruction layer (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/rules/). Discovers all instruction files in the repo, extracts semantic maps, and surfaces contradictions, shadowing, gaps, and drift before they cause expensive agent misbehavior. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: tribunal
plugins.desc: Multi-agent execution with LLM-as-a-Judge quality gates. An Actor performs work; a jury of typed Judges scores it against a project-overridable rubric; a Meta-Judge reviews the jury for bias; the gate decides accept, retry, or exhaust. Grounded in LLM-as-a-Judge (Zheng et al. 2023) and LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge (Wu et al. 2024). Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: echo
plugins.desc: Prompt-change regression detection. When a watched agent file is modified, Echo runs a single-judge quality pass via claude -p and compares the score against a stored baseline to report improved, degraded, or neutral. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: governor
plugins.desc: Resource governance and budget enforcement. Tracks per-session token and cost spend, gates Task spawns before they exceed a configurable budget ceiling, and emits governor.* events for audit. Named for the steam-engine governor — a device that regulates output. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: compass
plugins.desc: Pre-write intent clarity gate. Intercepts write-class tool calls and requires a confidence threshold before allowing them to proceed. Evaluates the pending write against the prior assistant turn as context to avoid false positives on question-answer turns. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: scribe
plugins.desc: Intent documentation from agent activity. Captures why changes were made — problem context, decisions, tradeoffs — and distills them into readable artifacts at session end. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: counsel
plugins.desc: Weekly synthesis and recommendations from the full observability stack. Reads all plugin event logs, produces a structured improvement brief, and injects it at session start when the last brief is stale. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: warden
plugins.desc: Untrusted-content gate. Scans content flowing in through WebFetch and Read for prompt-injection patterns, and when a threat is detected closes a session-scoped gate that blocks Write, Edit, and Bash until the user explicitly clears it. Grounded in Meta's Agents Rule of Two: an agent should hold no more than two of {private data, external actions, untrusted content} at once — warden removes the external-actions property while untrusted content is in play. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: librarian
plugins.desc: Consolidation layer between archivist's per-session artifacts and the user's durable typed memory store. Detects which session decisions, dead-ends, and open questions deserve to live across sessions, classifies them into the user/feedback/project/reference types, and queues them as proposals for explicit confirmation. Auto-promotion is opt-in. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: curator
plugins.desc: Maintenance layer for the user's typed auto-memory store. At every SessionStart, runs four cheap heuristic checks (date_decayed, path_broken, broken_index, orphaned_memory) against the memories at ~/.claude/projects/<encoded>/memory/ inside a wall-clock budget. Surfaces findings as a one-line pointer to /curator review; never edits the memory store directly. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: historian
plugins.desc: Episodic memory layer. At SessionEnd, chunks and sanitizes the session transcript and stores chunks under $ONLOOKER_DIR/historian/<project-key>/sessions/ (default $HOME/.onlooker). On UserPromptSubmit, embeds the prompt and performs similarity retrieval over stored chunks to surface relevant past context. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: assayer
plugins.desc: Claim verification. At session end, parses the agent's final message for testable claims ("I ran the tests, they pass", "the build is green") and checks each against the actual command results in the session transcript, classifying it corroborated, contradicted, or unverifiable. Catches lying-without-malice. Advisory by default. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: bursar
plugins.desc: Multi-session, per-project budget accounting. Rolls each session's spend into a per-project ledger on SessionEnd and surfaces "this project burned $X this week" at SessionStart. Where governor regulates a single session, bursar is the cross-session rollup: it reads governor.session.complete off the shared event bus and degrades to a session count when governor is absent. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: lineage
plugins.desc: Per-change provenance — answers "why does this line exist?". Records session/turn metadata plus a secret-redacted, size-capped snippet for every Edit/Write/MultiEdit at PostToolUse into a per-project change ledger, then traces a file or line back to the change that introduced it by joining records to the transcripts historian preserves. Emits lineage.* events for audit. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community

plugins.name: inspector
plugins.desc: Per-edit lint and typecheck gate. Runs the project's configured checks on just the touched file after every Write/Edit/MultiEdit, so the agent sees its own lint and type errors before claiming success. Cheaper than running the full project verify; complements assayer (which catches the agent lying about claims). Emits inspector.* events for downstream analysis. Requires the ecosystem plugin.
plugins.author: Onlooker Community
